None of these lines involve command substitution, function definitions, or execution of external commands (e.g., `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, `exec`, etc.).

The `source` array references a GitHub release URL and two local files, which is standard for binary packages. The checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', indicating integrity verification is intended. Even if they were skipped, that alone would not make sourcing the file unsafe for `--printsrcinfo`. There is no evidence of malicious code execution during the sourcing phase. All content in the global scope is declarative and consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.

Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe, as it will not trigger any active payload or network activity at parse time.
</details>
